pr_title: System data streams are not being upgraded in the feature migration API
pr_body:
This commit adds support for system data streams reindexing. The system data stream migration extends the existing system indices migration task and uses the [data stream reindex API](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/8.x/data-stream-reindex-api.html).
The system index migration task starts a reindex data stream task and tracks its status every second. Only one system index or system data stream is migrated at a time. If a data stream migration fails, the entire system index migration task will also fail.
 
Closes: ES-10934
Closes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/122949
pr_comments: Hi @alexey-ivanov-es, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

OK, I think I see two bugs here, one minor and one less so. First, the minor one:
I see this in my logs about half the time I do an upgrade:
```
[2025-03-07T14:00:12,920][ERROR][o.e.c.m.SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeService] [v7.17.28-1] System index metadata upgrade failed java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "org.elasticsearch.cluster.metadata.IndexMetadata.getIndex()" because "indexMetadata" is null
        at org.elasticsearch.server@8.19.0-SNAPSHOT/org.elasticsearch.cluster.metadata.SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeService.shouldBeSystem(SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeService.java:171)
        at org.elasticsearch.server@8.19.0-SNAPSHOT/org.elasticsearch.cluster.metadata.SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeService$SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeExecutor.updateIndices(SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeService.java:242)
        at org.elasticsearch.server@8.19.0-SNAPSHOT/org.elasticsearch.cluster.metadata.SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeService$SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeExecutor.execute(SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeService.java:209)
        at org.elasticsearch.server@8.19.0-SNAPSHOT/org.elasticsearch.cluster.service.MasterService.innerExecuteTasks(MasterService.java:1075)
        at org.elasticsearch.server@8.19.0-SNAPSHOT/org.elasticsearch.cluster.service.MasterService.executeTasks(MasterService.java:1038)
        at org.elasticsearch.server@8.19.0-SNAPSHOT/org.elasticsearch.cluster.service.MasterService.executeAndPublishBatch(MasterService.java:245)
        at org.elasticsearch.server@8.19.0-SNAPSHOT/org.elasticsearch.cluster.service.MasterService$BatchingTaskQueue$Processor.lambda$run$2(MasterService.java:1691)
        at org.elasticsearch.server@8.19.0-SNAPSHOT/org.elasticsearch.action.ActionListener.run(ActionListener.java:452)
        at org.elasticsearch.server@8.19.0-SNAPSHOT/org.elasticsearch.cluster.service.MasterService$BatchingTaskQueue$Processor.run(MasterService.java:1688)
        at org.elasticsearch.server@8.19.0-SNAPSHOT/org.elasticsearch.cluster.service.MasterService$5.lambda$doRun$0(MasterService.java:1283)
        at org.elasticsearch.server@8.19.0-SNAPSHOT/org.elasticsearch.action.ActionListener.run(ActionListener.java:452)
        at org.elasticsearch.server@8.19.0-SNAPSHOT/org.elasticsearch.cluster.service.MasterService$5.doRun(MasterService.java:1262)
        at org.elasticsearch.server@8.19.0-SNAPSHOT/org.elasticsearch.common.util.concurrent.ThreadContext$ContextPreservingAbstractRunnable.doRun(ThreadContext.java:1044)
        at org.elasticsearch.server@8.19.0-SNAPSHOT/org.elasticsearch.common.util.concurrent.AbstractRunnable.run(AbstractRunnable.java:27)
        at java.base/java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1095)
        at java.base/java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:619)
        at java.base/java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:1447)
```
Here's why I think it happens:

- I have a system data stream, `.fleet-actions-results` that was created in v7. I run /_migration/system_features in 8.19.
- The system migration sees that it needs to upgrade the fleet data stream `.fleet-actions-results`.
- The system migration calls the reindex data stream API.
- When the reindex data stream API finishes, it swaps the new index into the `.fleet-actions-results data stream`, and the old one out. This creates a cluster state change
- The system migration sees the cluster state change since SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeService is a ClusterStateListener. It sees that there is a v7 system index named `.ds-.fleet-actions-results-2025.03.07-000001` that is not in a data stream. This is a system index that we need to update!
- The reindex data stream API deletes `.ds-.fleet-actions-results-2025.03.07-000001` now that we no longer need it
- The system migration API is attempting to reindex `.ds-.fleet-actions-results-2025.03.07-000001`. But it has been deleted. So we get the exception above.

This exception is harmless. It's just happening because the index has been deleted in between when we decided we needed to handle it and when we went to handle it. I think we ought to just have [SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeExecutor::updateIndices to continue in the for loop if indexMetadata is null](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeService.java#L243).

The other bug I think I'm seeing is that system indices become unreadable after upgrade. If I try to read `.fleet-actions-results` before the upgrade (with a header saying that I am the fleet product), it works fine. After doing an upgrade, making requests to the same index in the same way returns:
```
{"error":{"root_cause":[{"type":"illegal_argument_exception","reason":"Data stream(s) [.fleet-actions-results] may not be accessed by product [fleet]"}],"type":"illegal_argument_exception","reason":"Data stream(s) [.fleet-actions-results] may not be accessed by product [fleet]"},"status":400}
```
I think the problem is that [system data streams can only have indices starting with `.ds-<data_stream_name>-`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/indices/SystemDataStreamDescriptor.java#L134.), but the upgrade replaces the original index with one named `.migrated-ds-.fleet-actions-results-2025.03.07-000001`.

> My only remaining question with respect to design is whether we do/should add a block to the datastream to prevent write loss during a migration?

As I understand - no. The first step in data stream migration is to do a rollover, which creates a new write index for the data stream and all write requests will be send to it. And this new index was created with the current version, so doesn't need migration. @masseyke correct me if I'm wrong

issue_context.title: System data streams are not being upgraded in the feature migration API
issue_context.body: See https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/211614 for an example of what this looks like to the end user. We have a system data stream, `.fleet-action-results` that has one or more old backing indices. The user calls the feature migration API (`POST /_migration/system_features`), which is supposed to upgrade all system indices and data streams. That does not return any errors. Then the deprecation info API (`GET /_migration/deprecations`) tells them that they need to reindex the `.fleet-action-results` data stream (`POST _data_stream/_modify`). Since it is a system data stream though, the user is not allowed to reindex it. They get stuck in a position where they cannot upgrade.

review_comments: Ugly solution, if you see more elegant one please don't hesitate to suggest
Why is this no longer needed?

At 1198 of this file `feature.getIndexDescriptors()` has changed to `feature.getSystemResourceDescriptors()` which includes both indices and data streams. The rest of the removed code was essentially the same as there, so now remaining code covers both indices and data streams.
Should this be at the warn level?

I don't think so. This code should only execute in one scenario: the migration of a data stream starts -> the [child task](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/8.x/x-pack/plugin/migrate/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/migrate/task/ReindexDataStreamPersistentTaskExecutor.java#L52) migrating the data stream fails for some reason -> the user restarts the system indices migration task.

Since the data stream migration task [retains](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/8.x/x-pack/plugin/migrate/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/migrate/task/ReindexDataStreamPersistentTaskExecutor.java#L295) its status for 1 day, we need to "cancel" the existing task and start a new one to avoid getting the same failure result again. In this case, the failure has already been logged.
"Canceling" the task here is part of normal operation, so I don't think it should be logged as error or warning.  I don't even want to make it info as it might be confusing to see
Thanks for renaming this to something sensible
IIUC, this doesn't block the datastream from receiving writes while the migration is in progress.  Should it?
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/123926#issuecomment-2715421657

Could this go into an infinite recursive loop if another part of the system is causing persistent errors? e.g. `migrateDataStream()` -> `checkDataStreamMigrationStatus()` -> `cancelExistingDataStreamMigrationAndRetry()` ->  `cancelDataStreamMigration()` -> `migrateDataStream()` -> ...
(I may be missunderstanding the flow control here)

In the original system index migration logic, an error would just stop the whole migration from continuing, such that a user would need to retry.  I spoke with @gwbrown, who mentioned that this was intentional in case there was a failure elsewhere in the system.  WDYT?

It shouldn't. The chain `migrateDataStream()` -> ... -> `cancelExistingDataStreamMigrationAndRetry()` is possible if a task for migrating that data stream already exists and is in a failed state. In that case, we cancel it and start a new one.
A new task is only started if the cancellation is successful. This means we shouldn't receive a `ResourceAlreadyExistsException` (line 649), which means that `checkDataStreamMigrationStatus` is called with `restartMigrationOnError=false` (line 647).

There is still slight possibility that we end up at the line 714 not because of exception from `dataStreamMigrationFailed` (lines 701 and 703), but because of another error, I will try to improve handling there.

>an error would just stop the whole migration from continuing

Logic here is similar to deleting existing index created during failed migration attempt

> Logic here is similar to deleting existing index created during failed migration attempt

Yeah that makes sense and it's a good idea to retry.  

>There is still slight possibility that we end up at the line 714 not because of exception from dataStreamMigrationFailed (lines 701 and 703), but because of another error, I will try to improve handling there.

Exactly.  I'm worried that an issue in some other part of ES might cause this to just loop forever.

>Exactly. I'm worried that an issue in some other part of ES might cause this to just loop forever.

Should be fixed now

This request is cancellable if you give it the parent task id. I don't think that system index migration is cancellable though, right? I assume that's by design since most system indices and data streams are small, so no need to be able to cancel this?

> I don't think that system index migration is cancellable though, right? I assume that's by design since most system indices and data streams are small, so no need to be able to cancel this?

Yes

SystemIndexMigrator uses `ParentTaskAssigningClient`, I believe it should set the parent task id to the requests

My understanding is that if someone tries to reindex a system data stream directly using the reindexing API without the necessary permissions, it will be blocked before any transport action is triggered. However, I haven't verified this - I'll check this tomorrow
